incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: high error rate detected for service=runtime-inference (alert=runtime_errors_high). Triggered at 2026-03-15T02:37:02Z
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident PD-48291 created, urgency=high, assigned to schedule=oncall-engineering. Link: https://pd.example/PD-48291
alex: ack'd in PD, pulling up dashboards now — taking lead.
priya: thanks alex, I'm on logs / traces. seeing a ~3m spike in 5xxs from a small subset of hosts (us-west-2a).
jon: adding context: autoscaler had a short flurry of scale-ups 02:34-02:36, could be related to cold start failures?
alex: good catch. I'm running `kubectl get pods -n runtime -o wide | grep us-west-2a` to see pod churn.
alex: paste: ```
POD runtime-worker-7f5 b/Running 3/3 10.0.42.11 us-west-2a
POD runtime-worker-3c2 CrashLoopBackOff 0/3 10.0.44.9 us-west-2a
```
priya: CrashLoopBackOff matches increased 5xx traffic to the router. investigating container logs for 3c2.
priya: log snippet: `E 02:33:54 model-alloc failed: cuda OOM when allocating buffer` — looks like a single GPU node had an OOM and restarted.
alex: can you confirm if it's a dedicated host or part of shared pool?
priya: shared pool, instance i-rt-xl-8gpu-04. There's a recent deploy? checking deploy bot...
pagerduty-bot: deploy-bot: deploy/runtime v2.14.1 finished at 2026-03-15T02:31:07Z to cluster=prod-us-west-2 (user=ci).
jon: so deploy preceded OOM by ~2 minutes. Could be a memory regression or changed batch sizes.
ops-oncall: If it's single-host OOM, we can cordon and drain to avoid noisy 5xxs while we investigate. Should we?
alex: yes cordon the problematic node, but want to make sure capacity remains. Priya, do we have spare capacity in us-west-2?
priya: we have 2 spare nodes across AZs; draining one will cause some cold starts but better than repeated 5xxs.
alex: doing `kubectl cordon i-rt-xl-8gpu-04` and `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets` now.
alex: :white_check_mark: node cordoned and pods evicted, autoscaler is bringing up replacement nodes to maintain desired count.
priya: I'm tailing the restarted pod logs: they started serving again at 02:39:10, errors dropped immediately.
jon: metric view: 5xx rate returned to baseline by 02:40:00. No broad region impact.
alex: PD notes: brief customer-facing errors observed from 02:33:50–02:39:50, mostly for a subset of requests that hit the affected pod. No sustained latency increase.
incident-bot: Incident auto-healed: alert=runtime_errors_high resolved at 2026-03-15T02:40:30 (duration=3m28s).
pagerduty-bot: PD-48291 auto-resolved by system (resolution_reason=issue_recovered).
ops-oncall: recommend postmortem? seems transient and tied to a node-level OOM after deploy. maybe add canary checks for model batch memory?
priya: agree — marking for a short RCA. I'll pull the deploy artifacts and compare memory config: `git rev-parse HEAD` -> `a7ef2b3`. Noting config change: default_batch_max went from 8 -> 12 in this deploy.
jon: ah that explains it. higher batch default + some larger prompt lengths = OOM risk. We should throttle batch size in runtime config and roll a patch.
alex: I'll patch the runtime config to cap at 8 and push a canary release to us-west before rolling globally.
alex: patch PR opened: https://git.example/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/1298 — rolling to canary now.
ops-oncall: handoff to next oncall in 30m — leave PD notes and link to PR. Any customer impacts to call out?
alex: No reported customer tickets. A small percentage of requests failed briefly; no SLA breach expected.
priya: logging: samples show model allocations spike ~2x median with batch_max=12 on longer prompts.
jon: action items: 1) revert/patch batch_max to 8 (alex) 2) add canary checks for allocation growth (priya) 3) add alert refinement to avoid single-node noise (ops-oncall).
alex: leaving a summary in the incident channel and updating PD notes. Handoff: @ops-oncall take it from here for follow-ups.
ops-oncall: ack, I'll track the PR and follow up with the release team. Closing thread after canary looks stable.
incident-bot: Note: This thread will be archived. If further paging occurs, PD will reopen an incident.
alex: :thumbsup: thanks all — quick triage and recovery.
__notes: Generated Slack thread representing a transient flapping alert triggered by a node-level OOM after a deploy; includes PD/incident-bot messages, ack, mitigation (cordon/drain), auto-resolve, RCA pointers and handoff. All fields are strings or list of strings per agents.md.
